assessments.recommendation: Monomaterial unreinforced polymer (e.g., ABS) without overmolded rubber grips.
assessments.rationale: Using a monomaterial unreinforced polymer facilitates high-quality recycling (ESPR Annex I parameter (d), page 79) and prevents the generation of inseparable composite waste (parameter (r), page 80). Avoiding overmolded elastomers prevents material contamination during shredding and recovery, reducing the environmental footprint of end-of-life treatment (parameter (m), page 33/80) and minimizing microplastic and nanoplastic release (parameter (p), page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use Phase and Ergonomics, which prefer overmolded rubber grips for user comfort and slip resistance, and composite polymers for high impact resistance and lightweighting.

assessments.recommendation: Threaded fasteners (screws) using standard, non-proprietary drive types (e.g., Torx).
assessments.rationale: Threaded fasteners allow non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly, which is essential for ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (ESPR Annex I parameter (c), page 79). This avoids permanent chemical or thermal bonding solutions that are highly detrimental to recycling and component recovery (parameter (e), page 79), thereby reducing waste generation (parameter (r), page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing stage, which prefers ultrasonic welding or adhesives to reduce assembly time, lower production costs, and achieve better dust/water sealing (IP rating).

options_evaluated: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with glued magnets
Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with mechanically secured, extractable magnets
assessments.recommendation: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with mechanically secured, easily extractable permanent magnets.
assessments.rationale: A BLDC motor has a longer technical lifetime, supporting refurbishment and remanufacturing (ESPR Annex I parameter (c), page 79). Mechanically securing the magnets instead of gluing them ensures they can be easily extracted at end-of-life, facilitating high-quality recycling and recovery of critical raw materials (parameter (d), page 79) without the energy-intensive thermal processes otherwise needed to break adhesive bonds (parameter (g), page 79).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing stage due to the higher complexity and cost of designing a motor with mechanically secured, removable magnets compared to standard glued assemblies.

options_evaluated: Passive cooling via open ventilation slots
Active cooling with a shaft-mounted fan
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling via open ventilation slots combined with a mechanical shaft-mounted fan, avoiding any potting compounds.
assessments.rationale: Avoiding thermal potting compounds or encapsulants prevents permanent contamination of the electronics and motor. Potting compounds are highly detrimental to reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling (ESPR Annex I parameter (e), page 79) because they cannot be cleanly removed, which increases the amount of hazardous waste generated at end-of-life (parameter (r), page 80) and worsens the environmental footprint of EoL treatment (parameter (m), page 33/80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use Phase and Reliability, as potting compounds protect internal electronics from moisture, dust, and mechanical vibration, extending tool life in harsh environments.

assessments.recommendation: Fully modular plug-and-play architecture with separate, easily separable functional blocks (battery, switch, motor, control PCB).
assessments.rationale: A fully modular design allows individual worn-out or failed components to be replaced or upgraded independently, directly facilitating ease of upgrading, reuse, and refurbishment (ESPR Annex I parameter (c), page 79). This architecture avoids solutions detrimental to recovery (parameter (e), page 79) and significantly reduces the amount of waste generated by preventing the disposal of entire functional tools due to single-point failures (parameter (r), page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Design and Manufacturing stages, as modular connectors and structural partitions increase the physical size, weight, and bill-of-materials cost of the screwdriver.

options_evaluated: Removable and standardized slide-on Li-ion battery pack
assessments.recommendation: Removable and standardized slide-on Li-ion battery pack.
assessments.rationale: An integrated battery pack is highly detrimental to EoL safety and recycling (ESPR Annex I parameter (e), page 79), as shredding intact tools with lithium batteries poses severe fire hazards. A removable battery pack allows safe, separate collection and high-quality recycling of battery cells to recover critical materials (parameter (d), page 79). It also enables the tool housing to be refurbished or reused independently of battery degradation (parameter (c), page 79).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Design stage, which may prefer an integrated battery to achieve a more compact, ergonomic handle design and lower manufacturing costs.
